There are issues with the photos, for sure. I'm not looking to analyze that. I just wanted to touch base on a couple things mentioned in the text of the image. Ambulances absolutely do turn their engines off. In my line of work it is not uncommon to see the crew inside the hospital for some length of time dropping off the patient, assisting with whatever code or alert they brought the patient in under, taking time to eat if it is a break time, etc. They frequently do get left on, but in a semi-enclosed area like many ambulance bays, it is asked to turn them off as build-up of exhaust fumes can effect other patients.

I will say I have never seen a compressed air line in an ambulance bay at a hospital, but I have seen backboards lined up outside. Ambulance crew may leave/forget their backboard after dropping off the patient, especially if they have to immediately respond to another call. Common practice is usually to line them up someplace near the ambulance bay and the next time that department comes by, they pick them up.

Both of those being said, The bottom left image looks more typical of what I would see at a hospital. The bottom right image looks like a garage. But I've never been to the hospital these photos were taken at so I do not know how it is actually set up there in reality.
